messages:
alex: Heads-up — ticket #5129 from FinRetail. Private/VPC deployment in ap-south reports API calls routed to us-east endpoints. Customer sees consistent 250–400ms extra latency.
suri: Ugh. Any evidence of SNAT/peering picking the wrong hub or proxy? Can you paste traceroute/curl headers?
alex: Repro from their VPC (redacted IPs):
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.5.11
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-region-served: us-east-1
```
traceroute shows hop to hub-proxy-3 (us-east) despite source ASN pref-> ap-south hub.
mike: support-bot linked the customer's routing config earlier: `vpc-peering -> hub-nat -> central-proxy` and they have an onprem SD-WAN to the hub too. Looks like proxy affinity TTL is low; fallback picks a different hub when capacity spikes.
jen: Could also be a healthcheck flapping on ap-south proxy, causing traffic to evacuate to us-east. Any recent autoscaling events for ap-south?
alex: Console logs show this sequence: `proxy-health ap-south: UNHEALTHY -> DEGRADED -> HEALTHY` over 7s at 2026-02-11T08:21:10Z. ops-bot showed a burst of connections then a cooldown.
ops-bot: [incident] ap-south-proxy-2 reported CPU 93% at 08:21:09Z; rotated traffic at 08:21:15Z. (automated note)
suri: That lines up. Problem is the routing policy is region-affinity but fallback policy doesn't respect source VPC peering preference; it picks any available proxy with capacity (us-east wins). We should: 1) confirm SNAT mapping for customer traffic 2) confirm proxy affinity TTL and prefer same-region hub when available.
mike: Quick check — from our side NAT logs show their source IP SNATed to 34.120.x.y which belongs to hub-us-east pool. So SNAT selection is happening pre-proxy and choosing us-east nat IP.
jen: How are we selecting SNAT IP? Last design doc: 'choose closest NAT pool by route priority, then round-robin'. If route priority has ambiguous longest-prefix due to BGP advertisements from SD-WAN, it could prefer us-east.
alex: Customer's BGP had both ap-south and us-east paths with same local-pref because their SD-WAN learned both. So route selection ambiguous. They prefer ap-south but SD-WAN announcement caused tie.
suri: Action items: (a) ask customer to prefer ap-south path or set local-pref on their side; (b) we push a fix to prefer SNAT pool tied to ingress interface when available; (c) temporary mitigation: add a sticky route rule for their org in ap-south hub.
jen: For (b) engineering: propose change to NAT allocator: if ingress peer ASN/vpc tag maps to preferred-region, select that pool even if radv metrics tie. Should be low-risk.
mike: I'll open eng-ticket and tag eng-runtime / eng-infra. Also will add a canary feature flag to flip behavior by org.
alex: I told customer the short-term workaround: modify SD-WAN local-pref to prefer ap-south or we can add org-scoped static SNAT in ap-south. They accepted. Logging the repro steps in the support ticket.
suri: Also add an alert to watch for proxy-health flaps + SNAT pool shifts per org — we missed correlation that would have auto-annotated the routing change.
alex: Thanks team. I'll follow up with ticket updates and paste eng-ticket ID when created.
support-bot: Created support ticket #5129 -> internal issue #ENG-6742. Notifications sent to eng-runtime.
mike: ENG-6742 opened: "SNAT allocator: prefer ingress-region pool when route tie -> prevent wrong-hub fallback". I'll link this thread.
alex: Closing loop — customer applied the SD-WAN local-pref change and latency dropped back to baseline within ~3 minutes. They verified model endpoints are served from ap-south. Will keep monitoring for 24h.
jen: Nice. Please add postmortem notes if we see recurrence.
